Linked guides retain each receipt's source scope, direct-oracle versus Rust-test distinction and separate zero-sized return-call compiler dependency. DoubleEndedIterator<T> pairs next_back with the same Iterator<T> remainder; both bounds are explicit and None from either end fuses both. Borrowed Rev swaps direction without eager pulls, allocation, item caching or cleanup. Selected leaves and Map/Filter/FilterMap/Chain propagate reverse support; Take/Skip/Zip/Enumerate remain forward-only and compose after Rev. All four registered reverse runtime tests pass on Linux x86_64 across two disjoint commands: 7740 independent model commands, primary/extra no-allocation contracts, four collection scenarios with seven full-address/size matched releases and two exact LNC0008 bound rejections. Selected finite leaves and existing O(1) collection remainders propagate through Rev/Map/Take/Skip/StepBy/Peekable, with no pulls, callbacks, item reads, host calls, allocation or cleanup during counts. StepBy distinguishes initial/later blocks and Peekable counts a cache without relaxing its source-resumption policy. Zip is excluded for borrowed-source aliases; Chain for unrepresentable sums. No Repeat, callback-dependent/nested, checked-index Enumerate or borrowed hash/tree implementation is added. Valid state, manual lifetimes and source/callback nonreentrancy remain required; no unchecked memory trust. All four exact-size library gates pass on native Linux x86_64 across two receipts: three nonmodel passes in 11.82 seconds (the same command records a model fixture visibility failure), then an isolated corrected model pass in 8.44 seconds. The independent sequence/deque model checks 10714 cases and 35922 steps across 18 modes; pure contracts add no memory syscalls, observed collection backings have full-address/size matched releases, and five invalid capabilities reject with LNC0008. The real sample-bytes app uses optional Rev/Skip/StepBy/Take and exact safe reservation while retaining checked appends; all four application tests pass in 9.44 seconds/95 cases, including two reached allocation denials. The refactored synchronous client passes all six groups/188 cases in 27.70 seconds; direct Exchange passes five groups/83 cases through separate 7.93- and 9.90-second receipts with unchanged production source. ext::http_server.note: Shared server Protocol and one-leaf plain Exchange, with Connection as a synchronous facade. Latched Head/Request/Rejected decisions, explicit Continue, atomic response staging, stable views until destroy, sticky fatal failures and retained rejection diagnostics are explicit. Abort retires transport while preserving backing; destroy releases backing. Canonical HTTP codecs remain the wire authority. Earlier sequential receipts retain their historical scope; concurrent handlers stage local views through the reply sink. The current plain app separately passes matrix 30, quota 1, limits 16, boundaries 25 and faults 41 across separate groups; these are 113 process-case invocations with known quota overlap, not 113 distinct cases. Faults reach 23 source-allocation positions. A separate actual plain-driver scheduler gate passes two reached poll-fault cases and one calibration: EINTR requires fresh publication and recovery without stale readiness, while EIO publishes PollIo(5), cleans live owners and preserves the caller listener.

These source metrics exclude native heaps, bootstrap, kernel memory and RSS. These 113 process-case invocations include the standalone quota repeated inside faults and are not distinct coverage. Historical sequential receipts retain their own scope. The thin serve_until helper does not require A:Destroy; both helpers pass a native empty-report transfer control with a non-Destroy application error type (21.84 seconds). The empty-report helper scope remains separate from the accepted three-profile populated E/A control.

Typed results preserve complete HTTPS diagnostics, input order, response ownership and partial outcomes. OpenSSL performs TLS and cryptography; callers establish SIGPIPE policy, and TLS 1.2/1.3 retry/closure scope follows https_client. All six connected groups pass 108 cases through three Linux x86_64/glibc/OpenSSL 3 receipts, including 42 reached source-allocation failures and six direct-step/abort controls. Plain batch separately passes eight groups/103 cases. The migrated HTTPS fetch passes four app groups/63 cases, and mutual-TLS application modes pass three groups/101 cases excluding prepared-context streams. Historical and current receipt scopes remain distinct; worker/server orchestration remains open.

Six focused groups pass 108 cases on Linux x86_64; application and plain-batch receipts have separate scopes.

Steps never poll; TLS uses stable staged writes, independent readiness needs and explicit TLS-call/I/O/deadline budgets. Early-final closure distinguishes TLS 1.3 notification from TLS 1.2 deferral; authenticated EOF is required for close-delimited bodies. Typed metadata preserves HTTP/TLS/cleanup diagnostics. Six connected HTTPS groups pass 108 cases across three native Linux x86_64/glibc/OpenSSL 3 receipts, including 42 reached source-allocation failures and six direct-step/abort controls. The migrated HTTPS app separately passes four groups/63 cases, and affected mutual-TLS app modes pass three groups/101 cases excluding prepared-context streams. These finite receipts do not establish every TLS schedule or another target. A confirmed 14-line nested enum-pattern reduction rejects with LNC0006; its explicit two-match x86_64 control executes all four assertions. No compiler or production transport change was needed for that expression spelling. The separate URL guide documents selected-socket adoption and Exchange.run, with eight current direct URL TLS cases kept separate from these historical numeric-driver counts.

ext::https_server.note: Shared server Protocol over OpenSSL 3 on Linux x86_64/glibc. Thirty-four direct native cases across seven groups pass through separate receipts: six verified steps, two early closures, four fatal-preparation/abort cleanup, four normal-close cleanup, six constructor/quota, four constructor-allocation and eight paired TLS 1.2/1.3 teardown cases. The teardown receipt is 21.05 seconds and checks missing-alert timeout, a cut native record, drain-cap overflow, authenticated empty input, pre-exit release and sticky replay. Cleanup groups each reach two close EIO injections; constructor allocation reaches three dynamic source failures, excluding native OpenSSL heap allocations. begin_connected consumes its accepted nonblocking socket on entry/error and eagerly creates a Session while ServerContext is borrowed; SSL_new retains the native reference. Steps never poll and perform zero or one active TLS attempt. HTTP events require verified handshake policy, stable writes survive WANT, and both protocol versions require local notify plus bounded discard to authenticated peer EOF before terminal publication. The raw 12-case closure experiment is distinct lower-layer evidence. SIGPIPE policy and manual ownership remain explicit; cryptography stays in OpenSSL. declarations.client: Requires a complete validated request without trailing bytes and the canonical 28-byte expected Accept computed for its original key. declarations.default_server_limits: Wire defaults plus 65536 bytes each for retained request, staged response and read budget, 65536 I/O attempts and 8388608 HTTP cursor work units. Validates response/buffer bounds and nested HTTP/wire limits before publishing the server.

std::atomic_file.note: Bounded sequential publication implemented in Lanius over TempFile and existing Linux descriptor calls. Replace/NoReplace commit syncs and closes the file once, renames once, immediately records Published/disarms deletion, then syncs the anchored directory. Receipts preserve NotPublished/Published/Unconfirmed visibility, confirmed bytes, current resources and separate primary/latest/cleanup errors. Native Linux x86_64/kernel 7.0.0-38-generic/ext4 under /tmp passes owner 9, bounds 25, publication 6 and faults 26: 66 process invocations across four groups including baselines; preliminary smoke overlaps. A live-anchor Published checkpoint precedes ACK-controlled explicit sync retry. The bounds retry fixes only the oracle owned-fd write selector and reuses the unchanged probe ELF. Thirty-six CPU ledger controls and Rust --no-run admission are separate from native execution. Actual source/fd ownership is observed before exit. Parent mutation authority must be exclusive/cooperative; attempts/bytes are bounded, blocking time is not. A failure can retain that Child authority unless ownership was lost or final reaping already occurred; captured output owners and child cleanup remain explicit. The guides define operation/deadline scope and current execution evidence.
